# math.answers.com

> > A comprehensive Q&A resource for solving math problems across arithmetic, algebra, geometry, and unit conversions with step-by-step explanations.

math.answers.com provides crowdsourced answers to mathematical questions ranging from basic arithmetic and fractions to advanced topics like rational exponents and 3D geometry. The site covers practical applications including percentage calculations, metric conversions, and number theory concepts.

## Key Topics

- Basic Arithmetic
- Fractions
- Percentages
- Unit Conversion
- Number Theory
- Least Common Multiple (LCM)
- Rational Exponents
- 3D Geometry
- Metric System
- Prime Factorization
- Math Problem Solving
- Statistics
- Q&A Format
- Step-by-Step Solutions

## Basic Arithmetic & Fractions

- [Three eighths plus one sixteenth?](https://math.answers.com/math-and-arithmetic/Three_eighths_plus_one_sixteenth): Q&A: Add fractions 3/8 and 1/16 with step-by-step solution
- [What is the LCM for 4 and 2?](https://math.answers.com/Q/What_is_the_LCM_for_4_and_2): Q&A: Find least common multiple (LCM) of 2 and 4

## Percentages & Statistics

- [What is 70 percent of 50000?](https://math.answers.com/statistics/What_is_70_percent_of_50000): Q&A: Calculate 70% of 50,000 using percentage formulas

## Geometry & Advanced Concepts

- [What 3d shape has all points on the surface that are the same distance from a given point?](https://math.answers.com/math-and-arithmetic/What_3d_shape_has_all_points_on_the_surface_that_are_the_same_distance_from_a_given_point): Q&A: Identify 3D geometry shape with equidistant surface points
- [What rational exponent represents a cube root taken to the fourth power?](https://math.answers.com/math-and-arithmetic/What_rational_exponent_represents_a_cube_root_taken_to_the_fourth_power): Q&A: Solve rational exponent problem with cube roots and powers

## Unit Conversions & Measurements

- [What is 10 hectares in meters?](https://math.answers.com/natural-sciences/What_is_10_hectares_in_meters): Q&A: Convert 10 hectares to square meters using metric system
- [How many centimeters to make a meter?](https://math.answers.com/natural-sciences/How_many_centimeters_to_make_a_meter): Q&A: Metric system conversion—100 centimeters equals 1 meter
